messages:
customer-joe: Hey team — priority ticket from Acme. They say streaming responses randomly fail mid-stream and the portal shows 5xx billing events. One sample request_id=rn-0a1b2c3d at 2026-03-16T21:34:12Z. Customer insists they closed client gracefully. Can we confirm whether this is our fault or client disconnect?
clara: Thanks, passing to runtime/SRE. Do we have the gateway logs for rn-0a1b2c3d? Any deploys around that time?
deploy-bot: deploy redwood/runtime v3.14.2 -> production completed at 2026-03-16T21:30:05Z :rocket: (sha abcdef)
liz: grabbing logs now. quick note — we have recent reports of chunked-encoding client-aborts being classified as 5xx in billing metrics. Might be related.
nate: can you paste the proxy + runtime log lines? Also need the raw request headers the customer sent if available.
customer-joe: Customer pasted this snippet:

-----
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Accept: text/event-stream
User-Agent: AcmeStreamer/1.2

<streaming payload>
-----

They say their client closed with ECONNRESET around 21:34:12 and saw a 5xx in portal.
priya: pasted runtime/gateway lines for rn-0a1b2c3d:

```
[2026-03-16T21:34:12.123Z] gateway: client_conn=12.34.56.78 req=rn-0a1b2c3d method=POST path=/v1/generate status=499 bytes=0 msg="client closed connection"
[2026-03-16T21:34:12.125Z] proxy: upstream_conn=10 status=502 reason="upstream reset" details="read ECONNRESET"
[2026-03-16T21:34:12.130Z] runtime: request=rn-0a1b2c3d stream_state=midstream teardown_reason=client_abort
```

priya: So the gateway marked client closed (499) in access log, proxy saw upstream reset -> 502, and runtime observed client_abort midstream. Looks like the underlying socket between runtime and proxy got RST after client closed, which made the proxy surface 502 to internal metrics.
clara: How are we mapping these events into billing classification today? I thought we translate 499-like client closes to non-billed events.
liz: current billing pipeline looks at the final internal status emitted by the proxy layer (502) if runtime had an upstream reset. For chunked streaming we sometimes see the proxy emit a 5xx metric even though the origin event was client_close. That causes customers to be billed and shows as 5xx in portal.
acct-billing: that's bad — customer gets a 5xx on their invoice. Can we filter upstream resets that follow immediate client_close within 200ms?
nate: We can, but need to be careful: sometimes upstream reset legitimately indicates runtime failure. Proposed heuristic: if gateway access log shows client_close (499-ish) and runtime stream_state==client_abort and upstream reset occurs within 500ms, mark as client-initiated (class 499) for billing.
priya: I reproduced locally with curl --no-buffer and a script that closes socket mid-chunk. Repro steps:

1) Start server with streaming endpoint
2) curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d @body.txt https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
3) After first few chunks, kill curl (kill -9)

Observed logs identical: gateway 499, proxy 502, runtime client_abort.

Snippet of repro client (python):
```
import requests, time, sys
r = requests.post(url, data=generator(), headers={'Transfer-Encoding':'chunked','Accept':'text/event-stream'}, stream=True)
for i, chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=None)):
    if i==3:
        sys.exit(0)  # abrupt client close
    print(chunk)
```

liz: filing a short-term mitigation: change billing pipeline to prefer gateway access log classification over proxy final status for streaming endpoints, with a backstop to flag suspicious patterns where runtime indicates an internal error. Will open RINF ticket.
clara: Please include customer-facing summary and whether we will credit charges.
acct-billing: customer eligible for credit if we confirm mis-billing. Hold any automated invoice escalations for Acme until we finish triage.

nate: Created ticket RINF-4321: "streaming: classify client aborts vs upstream resets in billing pipeline" assigned to runtime-team, priority P1. Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RINF-4321

priya: quick check — is there any evidence of recent CPU OOM or kernel socket issue on the node? Negative on all nodes in the window. Looks like normal client-initiated aborts.
liz: Action items: (1) short-term: adjust billing classifier to prefer gateway 499 for streaming endpoints (PR targeted for today), (2) medium-term: add telemetry to correlate gateway+proxy+runtime events into a single final-status event for metering, (3) follow-up: postmortem with metrics and customer credit plan.
clara: I told customer we'll issue a provisional credit and follow up with final resolution. Thanks all :heart:
acct-billing: I'll hold credit approval until RINF-4321 has the first PR.
